context.guidance: Do not write Personal Data or Authentication Secrets to localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies or outbound headers beyond what the session strictly needs. Keep identity in an opaque session identifier held server-side, and keep only non-Personal Data preferences in the browser. Where a value must be held client-side, protect it as Rule 6(1)(a) requires.

value.fix: Stop writing the auth token to localStorage. Delete `localStorage.setItem('token', authentication.token)` along with any matching `localStorage.getItem('token')` and `removeItem('token')` calls. Have the server keep the session and send only an opaque session ID to the browser, in a cookie set with `Set-Cookie: sid=<opaque-id>; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/`. Page scripts can't read that cookie, so an XSS bug can't steal it. On the client, send requests with `credentials: 'include'` for fetch or `withCredentials: true` for axios, and stop adding an `Authorization` header from stored values. If the SPA must hold a «SECRET», keep it only in memory, for example in a module variable or React context. Make it short-lived and renew it through an HttpOnly refresh-token cookie, never by persisting it in localStorage or sessionStorage. Also add CSRF protection, such as SameSite=Strict plus a CSRF token on requests that change state, and clear the token from the server-side session on logout.
